payload.claim: CLAUDE.md's Conventions section states a comment is one or two lines naming the non-obvious why, and that new comments take no semicolon (zero tolerance, enforced for new Markdown and new comments). The new `witness:` block comment at lines 33-36 is four lines long and line 34 reads "Each pattern's `name` group is a constant's name; a constant pattern's `value` group", containing a semicolon. Every sibling `FILL:` comment in this same file (lines 10, 23, 25, 27) is one line, so this block also breaks the file's own established convention. The `prose` gate cannot catch this: `.saffron/gates/prose.py`'s `in_scope` only admits paths ending in `.py` (under `CODE_DIRS`) or `.md` (under `ROOT_FILES`/`INCLUDED_DIRS`); a `.yaml` template is never read by it, so this violation reaches no gate.
